parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Yarrow
Yarrow is a community in Chilliwack, south of the Vedder River, and an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.

The closest official description is the City’s Yarrow Neighbourhood Plan material: the neighbourhood is bordered by Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land on all sides, by the Vedder River, the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve and Browne Creek Wetlands to the north, and by the BC Hydro Railway (Southern Railway of British Columbia) to the east.
The City says Yarrow covers about 175 hectares.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Yarrow

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The Yarrow Neighbourhood Plan was adopted by Council in 2022 and updated in 2025 as part of the Official Community Plan update. It is now Schedule B7 of the 2050 plan.
The City of Chilliwack’s 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, was adopted on December 16, 2025.
The City’s Engage Chilliwack page says Yarrow is outside the City’s Urban Growth Boundary and is planned under a minimal-growth scenario.
The 2040 Official Community Plan, which the 2050 plan replaced, listed Yarrow as a Rural Settlement, with a policy to retain its existing boundary and limit growth to existing development areas.
ALR: the village is bordered by ALR land on all sides. The Agricultural Area Plan, Schedule B1 of the 2050 plan, covers the farmland around it. ALR status is set parcel by parcel.
Flood and ground: Yarrow is flat, low-lying land, and the City says the water table is close to the surface.
The Vedder River borders the village on its north side, along with the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve and Browne Creek Wetlands.

City floodplain mapping is based on the Province’s Fraser River flood levels from the 1894 flood of record, which the City describes as roughly a 1-in-500-year flood. The City updated its floodplain maps in 2007. Property-level flood status is checked address by address.
The City of Chilliwack is one of the partners, with the Province, Abbotsford and three First Nations, in the Sumas River Flood Mitigation Collaborative Framework, signed on April 28, 2023.

Where is Yarrow?
Yarrow is a community in Chilliwack, south of the Vedder River, and an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.

The closest official description is the Yarrow Neighbourhood Plan material: bordered by ALR land on all sides, by the Vedder River, the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve and Browne Creek Wetlands to the north, and by the BC Hydro Railway to the east.
These edges are not an official boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Yarrow?
BC Transit route 55 Yarrow–Greendale runs a loop from Vedder Rd at South Sumas Rd to the UFV Chilliwack campus, Yarrow and Greendale, on weekdays and Saturdays.
Its timing points are Vedder Rd at South Sumas Rd, the UFV Chilliwack campus, Yarrow Central Rd at Kehler St and Greendale.
BC Transit’s 2024 Chilliwack and FVRD Transit Future Action Plan proposes restructuring and combining routes 55 and 59. Published municipal directories do not list a date for it.

route 55 page
Which school is in Yarrow?
Yarrow Community School (kindergarten to grade 5) is at 4595 Wilson Rd N.
The school’s website says Grade 5 students move to Stitó:s Lá:lém Totí:lt for Grade 6.
Use the official SD33 School Locator to confirm the secondary school. Check an exact address with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are in Yarrow?
Yarrow Pioneer Park (2.5 hectares) has a playground, a skate park, a picnic area and washrooms, and hosts the annual Yarrow Days event.
Yarrow Community Park (1.5 hectares) has tennis courts, basketball and a ball hockey area, and the Yarrow Library and Community Hall are in it.
Published municipal directories do not list a City leisure centre in Yarrow.
What plan covers Yarrow?
The Yarrow Neighbourhood Plan, adopted by Council in 2022, updated in 2025 and now Schedule B7 of the 2050 Official Community Plan.
The Engage Chilliwack page says Yarrow is outside the Urban Growth Boundary and planned under a minimal-growth scenario.
Is Yarrow in a floodplain?
Yarrow is flat, low-lying land, and the City says the water table is close to the surface.

City floodplain mapping is based on the Province’s Fraser River flood levels from the 1894 flood of record, which the City describes as roughly a 1-in-500-year flood. The City updated its floodplain maps in 2007.
Property-level flood status needs an address check with the City.
Do Yarrow homes have sewer, and is any of Yarrow in the ALR?

Homes in Yarrow have their own septic systems and are not on the City’s sanitary sewer. The Zoning Bylaw sets maximum gross floor areas for residential buildings to protect groundwater, and an accessory dwelling unit needs a satisfactory independent hydrogeological assessment.
The village is bordered by ALR land on all sides.
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
